audit.whatIsWrong: Hexplosive Minefield (E) is described in both layers purely as a zoning wall ('zones your approach', 'zones the ground you need to walk') with no mention of the clause that makes walking through it viable.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Successive mine detonations on the same target deal reduced damage.' The first mine is the expensive one and every mine after it costs Zac less. For a tank whose entire problem in this lane is crossing distance, that is the difference between the minefield being a wall and being a toll. It is a flat 16s cooldown, so a crossed field is also 16 seconds of clear ground.
audit.corrected: Successive mines on the same target deal reduced damage — the field zones far harder than it actually hurts you. 16s flat.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers are organised entirely around 'bait Satchel Charge' and neither ever states its cooldown, which is the one number the whole plan depends on.
audit.why: Satchel Charge is 20/18/16/14/12s. Because it is also his only self-peel, a spent Satchel is a 20-second window at rank 1 in which a squishy immobile mage has no answer to a committed Zac. That reframes it from a reactive warning into a countdown worth actually tracking. Bouncing Bomb is 6s, Mega Inferno Bomb 120s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Satchel Charge is 20s at rank 1 and is his only escape — once it is spent you have a 20-second kill window.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ziggs.json (Satchel Charge CD 20/18/16/14/12; Bouncing Bomb CD 6/5.5/5/4.5/4)

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer's phase chart gives Ziggs the '2+ items' stage while that same phase's own why text reads 'your side-lane pattern is at full power', and the content layer gives both late stages to Zac.
audit.why: phases[5].side is 'Skill' and phases[6].side is 'Ziggs', but content win[] is [...Ziggs, Zac, Zac] and the content late text calls this 'a hard-engage-onto-immobile-mage pattern that Zac wins decisively'. Zac's Emerald+ rate is 50.91% despite losing the entire laning phase, which only makes sense if the late stages are his. The full layer contradicts itself, the other layer, and the win rate simultaneously.

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither layer mentions that Satchel Charge displaces Ziggs himself, not just Zac.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'The explosion deals magic damage to enemies, knocking them away. Ziggs is also knocked away, but takes no damage.' It is simultaneously his knockback on Zac and his escape, which is why one W answers an engage twice over — and why baiting it is worth so much more here than a generic 'dodge his W'.
audit.corrected: Satchel knocks Ziggs away too — one cast both peels you and repositions him, so it is the only cooldown that matters.

edits.before: Ziggs pokes you out of the lane with Bouncing Bomb (Q) at long range while you have no way to close the gap pre-E; his Satchel Charge (W) knocks away your Elastic Slingshot engage and Hexplosive Minefield (E) zones your approach.
edits.after: Ziggs pokes you out with Bouncing Bomb (Q) on a 6s cooldown and Satchel Charge (W) knocks your engage away — but Hexplosive Minefield (E) deals reduced damage on successive detonations, so walking through it costs far less than the first mine implies.

edits.before: At 6 his Mega Inferno Bomb (R) adds global chip and waveclear, but this is where you flip it: once your E is up you can Slingshot onto him and his only escape is Satchel — bait the W and you have a kill.
edits.after: At 6 his Mega Inferno Bomb (R) adds global chip and waveclear, but this is where you flip it: Satchel is 20s at rank 1 and it is his only escape — bait the W and the next 20 seconds are a free kill.

edits.before: After your first tank item you can eat his poke and reach him; a landed E-Q-W plus knock-up bursts a squishy mage, and his cooldowns can't peel a committed Zac all-in.
edits.after: After your first tank item you can eat his poke and reach him; a landed E-Q-W plus knock-up bursts a squishy mage, and with Satchel spent he has no peel at all.

edits.before: Ziggs wins the early game on pure range: Bouncing Bomb (Q) chunks you from a screen away, Hexplosive Minefield (E) zones the ground you need to walk, and Satchel Charge (W) knocks you back if you try to close — with no gap-closer until E and no way to trade back, you just soak XP and take the poke.
edits.after: Ziggs wins the early game on pure range: Bouncing Bomb (Q) chunks you from a screen away every 6s, and Satchel Charge (W) knocks you back if you try to close. Note his minefield thins out — successive mines on the same target deal reduced damage — so it zones you far better than it actually hurts you.

edits.before: Through 3-6 he keeps poking, but the lane is turning: once your Elastic Slingshot (E) is online you can threaten to jump him, and his only answer is Satchel — so bait the W out, then engage, because a squishy Ziggs with W on cooldown dies to your E-W-Q burst and knock-up.
edits.after: Through 3-6 he keeps poking, but the lane is turning: once Elastic Slingshot (E) is online you can threaten to jump him, and his only answer is Satchel Charge on a 20s cooldown. Bait the W out, then engage — a squishy Ziggs with W down dies to your E-W-Q burst and knock-up.

edits.before: At 2 his Hexplosive Minefield (E) zones your approach and keeps you eating poke.
edits.after: At 2 his minefield zones your approach, though successive mines hurt less.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 his long-range poke keeps chipping you with no safe way to retaliate.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 his Bouncing Bomb chips you every 6s with no safe way to retaliate.

edits.before: Bait his Satchel Charge (W) before committing Elastic Slingshot (E)
edits.after: Bait his Satchel Charge (W), 20s at rank 1, before you commit E

edits.before: - Ziggs Satchel Charge: matchup-defining — His knockback + self-peel escape. Engage when it's down. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Ziggs Satchel Charge: 20/18/16/14/12s — his only escape, and it displaces him too, so bait it before you commit. - Bouncing Bomb: 6s. - Hexplosive Minefield: 16s, and successive mines on one target deal reduced damage. - Mega Inferno Bomb: 120s.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Satchel Charge's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: The lane-control window: Satchel Charge is 20s and is his only escape — bait it, then commit. If behind, farm safe and scale.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Ziggs carry threat 7.5/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items on: your engage beats a mage with no self-peel once Satchel is spent. Ziggs carry threat 7.5/10 — close it out.

edits.before: He kites you out — survive, then slingshot him on the Satchel Charge cooldown and out-sustain on blobs. Zac wins the Satchel Charge cooldown windows.
edits.after: He kites you out — survive, then slingshot him the moment his Satchel Charge (20s) is spent; his minefield zones far harder than it hurts.

edits.before: Trade strictly around Satchel Charge: when it is down, run your full pattern; when it is up, give nothing. If behind, farm safe and let your spikes re-open the lane.
edits.after: Trade strictly around Satchel Charge: it is 20s and his only escape, so when it is spent, run your full pattern. Successive mines deal reduced damage, so cross the field.

notes: The most useful finding here is that Hexplosive Minefield deals reduced damage on successive detonations against the same target — both layers presented the minefield as a hard wall, when for a tank crossing it is a toll that gets cheaper. Chart change proposed on the full layer only (phases[5].side and phases[6].side -> Zac): the full layer currently gives Ziggs the 2+ items stage while that phase's own why text says Zac's pattern is at full power, and the content layer already gives both late stages to Zac. These are short enum-ish cells, so the +/-10% length band needs an exemption for side labels or the edit will be rejected. Packet suspectName ("Let's Bounce" in spikes[3]) is a FALSE POSITIVE — the file writes "Let's Bounce!" and the detector strips the '!'. NOT VERIFIED and left alone: whether Satchel Charge's knockback can displace Zac out of his Elastic Slingshot charge or interrupt Let's Bounce!, and whether Zac's E can be knocked off-course mid-flight by it — this is the single most decision-relevant unknown in the matchup and worth one deliberate wiki check.
